n_nodes: <int> Total number of cities in the air transportation network, each serving as an origin, destination, and candidate hub location.
p: <int> Number of hubs the entering airline must open.
r: <int> Number of hubs operated by the competing incumbent airline.

nodes.x: <float> Horizontal spatial coordinate of the city.
nodes.y: <float> Vertical spatial coordinate of the city.
nodes.waiting_time: <float> Fixed layover delay passengers experience at this city's airport.

demand_matrix: <list[list[int]], shape [n_nodes][n_nodes]> Number of passengers wishing to travel from each origin city to each destination city.
distance_matrix: <list[list[float]], shape [n_nodes][n_nodes]> Euclidean distance between each pair of cities.
competitor_hub_locations: <list[int], length r> Node identifiers of the incumbent airline's fixed hub airports.

parameters.alpha: <float> Discount factor applied to the fare on the hub-to-hub leg of a two-hub route, reflecting economies of scale.
parameters.gamma: <float> Weight controlling how much passengers value travel time relative to fare when choosing a route.
parameters.beta: <float> Exponent governing how steeply route attractiveness decays with increasing travel time.
parameters.lambda: <float> Exponent governing how steeply route attractiveness decays with increasing fare.
parameters.cost_scalar: <float> Proportionality constant converting distances into fares.
parameters.attractiveness_2hub: <float> Base attractiveness value assigned to routes passing through two distinct hubs.
parameters.attractiveness_1hub: <float> Base attractiveness value assigned to routes passing through a single hub.
